3. This criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the entire criminal proceeding including the order dated 20.07.2022 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Palamau whereby and where under the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Palamau took cognizance for the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code against the petitioners in connection with Women Santosh Prajapati vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21834234/

sentences.text: 4. The brief fact of the case is that the petitioner no.1 being the husband, petitioner no.2 being the father-in-law and the petitioner no.3 being the mother-in-law of the informant, five years after her marriage tortured the informant mentally and physically for ten years thereafter and ultimately drove her out.
There is specific allegation of 25.01.2022 at 06:00 pm when the petitioners along with co-accused persons of the case assaulted the informant and drove her out from their house.
Hence she has been residing in her matrimonial house.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners drawing attention of this Court to page no. 36 which is the judgment of Complaint Case No. 164 of 2005 submits that thereby the petitioners were convicted for having committed the offences punishable under Sections 498A of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act vide judgment dated 03.08.2018 and the informant in that case stated that her marriage was solemnized in the year 1999 and in the year 2001 her donga was concluded and she went to her in-laws house and after remaining there for 15 days the husband and other family members called her kali kaloti and started demanding Rs.25,000/- It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners preferred Criminal Appeal No. 72 of 2018 and vide judgment dated 24.08.2022 in Criminal Appeal No. 72 of 2018, the sentence of the petitioner no.1 was modified from two years to one year with fine; whereas the conviction of the petitioner nos.2 and 3 were set aside and in this respect, learned counsel for the petitioners draws the attention of this Court to the copy of the certified copy of the judgment dated 24.08.2022 kept at page no. 48-54 of the brief.

It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the informant has filed the FIR by suppressing the material facts and modifying the allegations as though and admittedly, her marriage took place in 1999 but in this case in the year 2022 informant has stated that she married the petitioner no.1 fifteen years before that is in or around the year 2007.
It is then submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that there is no allegation in the present case about her being called kali kaloti or demand of Rs.25,000/-.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that in the absence of any allegation of harassment with a view to coercing the informant or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or on account of failure by the informant or any person related to her to meet such demand and in the absence of any allegation of any willful conduct on the part of the petitioners as is likely to drive the informant to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health whether mental or physical even if the allegation made in the FIR, the statement of the witnesses which has been mentioned in the case diary and other materials of the case diary as well as the charge sheet are considered to be true still the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code is not made out.

sentences.text: Coming to the facts of this case, upon a perusal of the contents of the FIR dated 1-4-2019, it is revealed that general allegations are levelled against the appellants.
The complainant alleged that "all accused harassed her mentally and threatened her of terminating her pregnancy".

Furthermore, no specific and distinct allegations have been made against either of the appellants herein i.e. none of theappellants have been attributed any specific role in furtherance of the general allegations made against them.
This simply leads to a situation wherein one fails to ascertain the role played by each accused in furtherance of the offence.
The allegations are, therefore, general and omnibus and can at best be said to have been made out on account of small skirmishes.
Insofar as husband is concerned, since he has not appealed against the order of the High Court, we have not examined the veracity of allegations made against him.
However, as far as the appellants are concerned, the allegations made against them being general and omnibus, do not warrant prosecution."
(Emphasis supplied)
and in the facts of that case, this Court quashed the entire criminal proceeding.

sentences.text: Their Lordships of the Supreme Court in Ramesh case [(2005) 3 SCC 507 : 2005 SCC (Cri) 735] had been pleased to hold that the bald allegations made against the sister-in-law by the complainant appeared to suggest the anxiety of the informant to rope in as many of the husband's relatives as possible.
It was held that neither the FIR nor the charge-sheet furnished the legal basis for the Magistrate to take cognizance of the offences alleged against the appellants.

The learned Judges were pleased to hold that looking to the allegations in the FIR and the contents of the charge-sheet, none of the alleged offences under Sections 498-A, 406 IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act were made against the married sister of the complainant's husband who was undisputedly not living with the family of the complainant's husband.

Their Lordships of the Supreme Court were pleased to hold that the High Court ought not to have relegated the sister-in- law to the ordeal of Santosh Prajapati vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21834234/

25. However, we deem it appropriate to add by way of caution that we may not be misunderstood so as to infer that even if there are allegations of overt act indicating the complicity of the members of the family named in the FIR in a given case,
cognizance would be unjustified but what we wish to emphasise by highlighting is that, if the FIR as it stands does not disclose specific allegation against the accused more so against the co-accused specially in a matter arising out of matrimonial bickering, it would be clear abuse of the legal and judicial process to mechanically send the named accused in the FIR to undergo the trial unless of course the FIR discloses specific allegations which would persuade the court to take cognizance of the offence alleged against the relatives of the main accused who are prima facie not found to have indulged in physical and mental torture of the complainant wife. It is the well-settled principle laid down in cases too numerous to mention, that if the FIR did not disclose the commission of an offence, the court would be justified in quashing the proceedings preventing the abuse of process of law.

Simultaneously, the courts are expected to adopt a cautious approach in matters of quashing, especially in cases of matrimonial disputes whether the FIR in fact discloses commission of an offence by the relatives of the principal accused or the FIR prima facie discloses a case of overimplication by involving the entire family of the accused at the instance of the complainant, who is out to settle her scores arising out of the teething problem or skirmish of domestic bickering while settling down in her new matrimonial surrounding."
and in the facts of that case, quashed the entire criminal proceeding qua the petitioners of that case only.

8. It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that in the absence of allegation of essential ingredients of Section 498A of Indian Penal Code even if the allegation made in the FIR and other materials collected during the investigation of the case as mentioned in the case diary as well as the charge sheet is considered to be true; still the offence punishable under section 498A, of the Indian Penal Code, is not made out.
Hence, it is submitted that the entire criminal proceeding including the order dated 20.07.2022 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Palamau be quashed and set aside.

9. Learned Special Public Prosecutor on the other hand opposes the prayer for quashing the entire criminal proceeding including the order dated 20.07.2022 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Palamau and submits that the materials in the record is sufficient to constitute the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code and the learned Magistrate has not committed any illegality by taking cognizance upon submission of charge sheet.
Hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.

4 10. Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that the essential ingredients to constitute the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code are :-
(1) a women was married (2) she was subjected to cruelty (3) such cruelty consisted in (i) any willful conduct as is likely to drive such woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger her life, limb or health (whether mental or physical)
(ii) harass to such woman with a view to coercing her to meet unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or on account of failure of such women or any of her relation to meet the unlawful demand.
(iii) the women was subjected to such cruelty by her husband or any relation of her husband.
11.

sentences.text: Now coming to the facts of the case, there is absolutely no allegation against the petitioners of committing any willful conduct as was likely to drive the complainant to commit suicide or any willful conduct which was likely to cause grievous injury to the victim or any willful conduct which was likely to endanger the life, limb or health, whether mental or physical, of the victim.

12. The undisputed fact also remains that earlier also for a different set of allegation including the period of this case, the informant instituted Complaint Case No. 164 of 2005 and in this FIR the same has been suppressed.
The time of marriage of the petitioner has been changed from 1999 to 15 years before 2022 which comes to around 2007.
There is no allegation of any demand of dowry in this case, unlike the earlier complaint filed by her.
13. It is a settled principle of law that it is the litigant's bounden duty to make a full and true disclosure of facts.

It is a matter of trite law, and yet bears repetition, that suppression of material facts before a court amounts to abuse of the process of the court, as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Krishna Lal Chawla & Others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh &
Another reported in (2021) 5 SCC 435 paragraphs-13 and 26 of which read as under :-

sentences.text:
It is also crucial to note that in the fresh complaint case instituted by him,
Respondent 2 seems to have deliberately suppressed the material fact that a charge- sheet was already filed in relation to the same incident, against him and his wife, pursuant to NCR No. 160 of 2012 (Crime No. 283 of 2017) filed by Appellant 1's son.
No reference to this charge-sheet is found in the private complaint, or in the statements under Section 200 CrPC filed by Respondent 2 and his wife.

In fact, both the private complaint and the statement filed on behalf of his wife,
merely state that the police officials have informed them that investigation is ongoing pursuant to their NCR No. 158 of 2012.
The wife's statement additionally even states that no action has been taken so far by the police.
It is the litigant's bounden duty to make a full and true disclosure of facts.

It is a matter of trite law, and yet bears repetition, that suppression of material facts before a court amounts to abuse of the process of the court, and shall be dealt with a heavy hand (Ram Dhan v.
State of U.P. [Ram Dhan v. State of U.P., (2012) 5 SCC 536 : (2012) 3 SCC (Cri) 237] ; K.D. Sharma v. SAIL [K.D. Sharma v. SAIL, (2008) 12 SCC 481] ).

State of U.P. [Ram Dhan v. State of U.P., (2012) 5 SCC 536 : (2012) 3 SCC (Cri) 237
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a settled canon of law that this Court has inherent powers to prevent the abuse of its own processes, that this Court shall not suffer a litigant utilising the institution of justice for unjust means.
Thus, it would be only proper for this Court to deny any relief to a litigant who attempts to pollute the stream of justice by coming to it with his unclean hands.
Similarly, a litigant pursuing frivolous and vexatious proceedings cannot claim unlimited right upon court time and public money to achieve his ends."
(Emphasis supplied)

14. In view of the discussions made above, this Court has no hesitation in holding that even if the allegations made against the petitioners are considered to be true in their entirety still the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code is not made out; coupled with the fact that the informant has suppressed the institution of the earlier Complaint Case No. 164 of 2005, this Court is of the considered view that continuation of the criminal proceeding will amount to abuse of process of law and this is a fit case where the entire criminal proceeding including the order dated 20.07.2022 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Palamau be quashed and set aside.
15. Accordingly, the entire criminal proceeding including the order dated 20.07.2022 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Palamau is quashed and set aside.
16. In the result this criminal miscellaneous petition is allowed.
